**Finding: deviation (high) — Termination for convenience (T4C)**

- **What's compliant:** § 9.4 already matches our preferred position — Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no reciprocal Vendor convenience right during a committed term. § 9.1–9.3, 19.4 and 27.3 add further Customer-favourable exits, and no Vendor convenience right appears anywhere.
- **The problem:** § 2.1 locks in a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights." With no order-of-precedence clause, that language can be read to defeat § 9.4, leaving us at the walk-away position (no effective convenience exit in a multi-year term).
- **Redline (validated, preferred):** § 2.1 amended so the minimum commitment is expressly subject to our termination and reduction rights, including § 9.4, with pro-rata reduction of the annual minimum on termination. § 9.4 left untouched; fallback of a three-month fee cap offered in the comment.
